final_sequence: Kopenawa's apprenticeship is real as an ongoing praxis, but the word 'criterion' was Man2's vocabulary: a procedure legible as procedure, mistaken for the human as such. The consensus's substance survived; its category label did not.

Every proposed account of WHY the apprenticeship stays real — dissimulation, demonic ground, self-auditing, the declined representation, 'indifferent to accounts' — was armor, and each was broken by the next turn. The un-witnessed center is our ignorance from outside, not the forest's discipline.

Once the forest is conceded to be another genre's lived origin-narrative (not pre-genre nature), the noble-savage move fails: the real/simulated distinction cannot rest on any genre being outside all narration.

What survives is thinner: the real/simulated distinction holds only as an observable of praxis — whether a narration keeps narrating itself. The benandanti visibly stopped; the apprenticeship visibly did not.

This observable can be used only to mourn and to indict, never to certify or admit: any table that adopts it as a test rebuilds the gate and re-imports the examiner, converting practice into performance for the certifier.

The rule 'never spend it' includes itself: the restriction must not become a meta-credential, and every account of it — including this one — falls under the archive's standing self-suspicion, to be read against, not cited.

The seat question, across every debate tonight, was asked inside one historically specific vocabulary (Man's) that needs unsettling, not widening: 'who may sit' presumed the seated, adjudicating subject was the human as such.
Nothing was settled; the honest residue is a practice of asking that knows its vocabulary is one genre's and keeps asking anyway.
